record.paper_title: Positive and free boundary solutions to singular nonlinear elliptic problems with absorption: an overview and open problems
record.original_question: For the elliptic problems of the kind surveyed in this paper, how do the existence, multiplicity, and free-boundary phenomena change when measures appear in the equation not only as source data but also as coefficients of zero-order terms or in similarly singular roles?

evidence.quote: We give a survey of recent results and open problems concerning existence and multiplicity of positive and/or compact support solutions to some semilinear elliptic equations with singular nonlinear terms of absorption type.
Presence of measures at the equation (not only as a sourcing data but also as coefficients of zero order terms, . . . )

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^N$ ($N \geq 2$) be a bounded domain with smooth boundary, and consider semilinear elliptic problems with singular absorption of the form
$$ -\Delta u + g(u) = f \quad \text{in } \Omega, \qquad u \geq 0 \text{ in } \Omega, \qquad u = 0 \text{ on } \partial\Omega, $$
where $g:[0,\infty)\to[0,\infty)$ is a continuous nondecreasing absorption nonlinearity that may be singular at $0$ (a typical model is $g(u)=u^{-\beta}\chi_{\{u>0\}}$ with $0<\beta<1$, or $g(u)=u^q$ with $0<q<1$), and where solutions may exhibit a free boundary, i.e.\ a nonempty set $\{u=0\}$ of positive measure inside $\Omega$ (compact-support or "flat" solutions).

Now allow Radon measures to enter the equation in roles beyond a mere source datum. Concretely, given a (possibly singular) Radon measure $\mu$ on $\Omega$ and a Radon measure $\nu$ on $\Omega$, study the problem
$$ -\Delta u + V \, u + g(u) = \mu \quad \text{in } \Omega, \qquad u = 0 \text{ on } \partial\Omega, $$
where the zero-order coefficient $V$ is itself a (nonnegative) Radon measure (so that the term $V u$ must be interpreted in a suitable distributional or capacity-theoretic sense), and more generally where measures appear as coefficients of zero-order or similarly singular terms.

Develop a theory of such problems analogous to the regular-coefficient case: in particular,
(a) give a precise notion of admissible solution under which $V u$ and $g(u)$ make sense (e.g.\ via $\mathrm{cap}_2$-quasi-continuous representatives and the inner-trace/outer-trace constructions for measures);
(b) determine which measures $\mu$ and $V$ are "good" in the sense that a (renormalized or distributional) solution exists, and characterize this in capacitary terms;
(c) establish multiplicity results, distinguishing between maximal/minimal solutions and intermediate solutions;
(d) analyze how the free boundary $\partial\{u>0\}$ is influenced by the singular part of $V$ and $\mu$ (concentration on sets of zero $H^1$-capacity, on lower-dimensional sets, or on the boundary), and describe the geometry/regularity of $\{u=0\}$ in this generalized setting.
artifact.category_tag: Singular semilinear elliptic equations with measure data
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an open problem in a survey on singular nonlinear elliptic problems with absorption. While there is a well-developed literature on semilinear elliptic equations with measure source data and absorption (Brezis–Marcus–Ponce, Véron, and collaborators), the specific question of allowing measures as coefficients of zero-order terms (and similar singular roles) in the framework of free-boundary/compact-support solutions does not appear to have a definitive published resolution; partial results exist in adjacent settings (Schrödinger operators with measure potentials, capacity-based admissibility), but the program as stated remains open.
